subject.title: fix: unify macos dashboard auth startup

question: Should the macOS embedded Dashboard browser receive native/stored device tokens, or should browser injection be limited to configured shared token/password auth?
rationale: The two open PRs implement conflicting credential boundaries on the same Dashboard path, and automation cannot safely choose whether native device tokens may cross into browser Control UI auth.

options.title: Resolve the browser-auth boundary first
options.body: Pause merge until a maintainer picks the Dashboard auth boundary, then update this PR or the sibling shared-token-only PR to implement that single policy with proof.

options.title: Accept native-token parity
options.body: Allow the embedded Dashboard to receive native/stored device tokens and document why the browser injection boundary is intentional.

options.title: Prefer shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Close or replace this PR in favor of the sibling direction that excludes native device-token fallbacks from browser injection.

recommendation.title: Resolve the browser-auth boundary first
recommendation.body: Pause merge until a maintainer picks the Dashboard auth boundary, then update this PR or the sibling shared-token-only PR to implement that single policy with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The central Dashboard window and recent transport hardening history point to this owner as the best available decision route.
